answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity commits a hash of its action history per epoch; the next epoch must present actions statistically consistent with that trajectory. An identity drifting from its own past—as clones do when copied across an ocean of records—fails the consistency check and loses accumulated reputation. Attackers must maintain coherent histories per clone across epochs, a ferrous discipline of continuous distinct behaviour. The knoll of entry is low but each sustained clone demands separate genuine activity, multiplying attacker workload linearly per identity.
